_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The EPA RMP regulation requires that an Executive Summary be provided as part of the registration submitted to the EPA. 
Note: This summary includes additional information not included in the RMP Submit to assist California Dairies Inc. management, process operators, technicians, contractors plus all involved and affected employees towards safe operation. In addition, some of the detail provided within this summary was excluded from the submitted RMP as current public access to this detail could expose the facility and personnel to terrorist or criminal activity.

California Dairies Inc. prepared a Chemical Risk Management Program and Process Safety Management Program (RMP/PSM) in general accordance with state and federal regulations. The state risk management regulations, also referred to as the California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) program, are codified in California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 19, Section 2745, et. seq. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) also regulates facilities with certain toxic and flammable substances. The federal regulations are codified in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Title 40, Section 68. Finally, both the California Occupational Safety and Health Administration (CalOSHA) and the federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulate facilities with certain acutely hazardous materials under the PSM standards as defined in CCR, Title 8, Section 5189 and CFR Title 29, Part 1910, Section 119, respectively.

The following areas are addressed in this summary:
1.	Accidental release prevention and emergency response policies 
2.	The stationary source and regulated substances handled
3.	The accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps
4.	The five-year accident history
5.	The emergency response program
6.	Planned changes to improve safety

C-1   ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES 
California Dairies Inc. is committed to complying with all th

e regulatory requirements of the EPA Risk Management Program.  California Dairies Inc. has developed their Risk Management Plan / Process Safety Management (RMP/PSM) making up the CalARP program to document policies and address the implementation of these regulations. The PSM sections pertain to the prevention of accidental releases and include the Process Hazard Analysis study and procedures for operating, training, maintenance, emergency response, and others. The RMP sections pertain to management systems and include the Hazard Assessment (Offsite Consequence Analysis) Report.

In the unlikely event that a chemical release does occur at the facility, California Dairies Inc. personnel are trained in the appropriate mitigation measures, relying on emergency services provided by local response agencies. California Dairies Inc. will continue to improve ammonia-handling safety through the implementation of the prevention program elements of the RMP/PSM program.

C-2   STATIONARY SOURCE ACTIVITIES AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES HANDLED
The California Dairies Inc facility provides product cooling, and short-term storage for milk and associated milk products and by-products. The stationary system (engine room) is operated 24 hours /7 days a week throughout the year to meet production needs. 

The facility is in Tulare County on a contiguous property right off the 99 Freeway.  Anhydrous ammonia is used as the refrigerant (Process 1) in the refrigeration system.  

C-3	RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM
To minimize the potential for accidental releases, California Dairies Inc. has implemented a comprehensive prevention program consistent with the elements required under RMP,  CalARP, and PSM regulations. Key components include:

	Process Safety Information (PSI):
Complete and accurate written information is maintained on the hazardous properties of regulated substances, the design basis and configuration of process equipment, and the technology of the processes. This information is used

as a foundation for safe operation and hazard evaluation.

	Process Hazard Analysis (PHA):
A thorough hazard analysis is conducted for each covered process using approved methodologies (e.g., What-If/Checklist, HAZOP, FMEA). PHA studies are updated and revalidated at least every five years. Recommendations are prioritized, tracked, and resolved.

	Operating Procedures:
Written procedures are maintained and reviewed annually for all operations including startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, and normal shutdown. These procedures ensure consistent and safe process operation.

	Training:
Operators and maintenance personnel receive initial and refresher training on process safety, operating procedures, and emergency response. Training effectiveness is verified through testing or demonstration of competency.

	Mechanical Integrity:
Critical process equipment, including pressure vessels, piping systems, relief devices, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and sensors, is subject to a preventive maintenance program. Equipment is inspected and tested following recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices (RAGAGEP).

	Management of Change (MOC):
Changes to process chemicals, technology, equipment, procedures, or facilities are evaluated for potential safety impacts before implementation. The MOC system includes requirements for authorization, documentation, and training of affected personnel.

	Pre-startup Safety Review (PSSR):
Prior to startup of new or modified equipment/processes, a safety review is performed to ensure that construction is in accordance with design specifications, procedures are in place, training is completed, and recommendations from PHAs and MOCs are addressed.

	Compliance Audits:
A comprehensive compliance audit is conducted at least every three years to evaluate the effectiveness of the prevention program. Deficiencies identified during the audit are promptly corrected and documented. Note: Thi

s is not a PSM requirement; this is addressed in the IIPP.

	Incident Investigation:
All incidents that resulted in or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release are investigated. The root cause is identified, and corrective actions are developed, implemented, and communicated to affected personnel.

	Employee Participation:
Employees are actively involved in the development and implementation of the prevention program. The written participation plan ensures timely access to relevant safety information and involvement in PHAs and other safety activities.

	Hot Work Permits:
A formal permitting system is used for hot work operations conducted on or near covered processes. Permits are issued only after fire prevention and protection measures are confirmed to be in place.

	Contractor Safety Management:
Contractors who work on or near covered processes are evaluated for safety performance, informed of process hazards, and trained on applicable emergency response and safe work practices. Contractor activities are monitored to ensure compliance with safety policies.

C-4	FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
The CalARP regulations require a review of the 5-year accident history at the regulated facility. History must include "all accidental releases from covered processes that resulted in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage onsite, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage." California Dairies Inc. assured no reportable release of ammonia has occurred during the past 5 years (2020-2025).

C-5	EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
California Dairies Inc. maintains a written Emergency Response Plan (ERP) as directed by the UPA. The facility only takes defensive actions for an incidental release in order to protect employees, environment and property. This plan is designed to ensure a prompt, coordinated, and effective response to accidental releases of regulated substances. Key features include:

	Emergency Planning and Coordination: Coordination with local emergency response agencies, including the local fire department and hazmat team, and other relevant authorities.

	Notification Procedures: Clearly defined procedures for immediate notification of appropriate emergency responders, the public (if necessary), and regulatory agencies in accordance with applicable release reporting requirements.

	Response Procedures: Guidance for personnel response actions, including evacuation and mitigation procedures.

	Training and Drills: Designated emergency response personnel are trained in accordance with OSHA HAZWOPER (29 CFR 1910.120) and applicable state standards. Drills and exercises are conducted to test and improve the plans effectiveness.

	Emergency Equipment: Adequate response equipment is maintained, routinely inspected, and readily available for use by trained personnel.

California Dairies Inc. will rely on outside responders from the fire department and the Tulare  County HazMat Team for mitigation of releases. The ERP states that the California Dairies Inc. Emergency Coordinator will be in charge until such time as an outside responding agency assumes that role. California Dairies Inc. management will oversee evacuation and remain in control until the Fire Department arrives, then Incident Command will be assumed by the senior Fire Department official at the scene. The Fire Department Incident Commander will be responsible for issuing notices for public evacuation and/or sheltering in place, if necessary. California Dairies Inc. management will be responsible for making initial contact with the Fire Department via 9-1-1; Tulare County UPA; CalOES, federal NRC, and any other agencies that need to be contacted. California Dairies Inc. will rely on community responders for medical assistance as necessary. Responsibility for cleanup after the release is spelled out in the ERP.

C-6	PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
California Dairies Inc. is dedicat

ed to continuous improvement of its accidental release prevention and emergency preparedness programs. We actively evaluate new regulatory developments, industry best practices, audit results, and incident learnings to ensure that our policies remain effective, current, and protective of our employees, community, and environment. Management responses and support will be consistent with California Dairies Inc.'s commitment to safe and environmentally responsible operations.

California Dairies Inc. recognizes that the RMP/PSM is a continuous process for evaluating, monitoring, and improving the handling of acutely / extremely hazardous chemicals and operations at its facility. As such, this document and related program elements will evolve as California Dairies Inc. continue their ongoing focus and dedication of risk minimization and safety improvement for their employees and surrounding community. 

California Dairies Inc. will submit revised information if a change occurs that is considered significant and requires resubmission under the regulations. However, minor improvements / modifications to the RMP/PSM, related attachments, and program elements will be incorporated consistently with California Dairies Inc.'s internal review practices, and California Dairies Inc. will maintain the most current versions onsite. Thus, the most current version RMP/PSM and related documents and elements maintained onsite may vary slightly from the information in submittals made to EPA and other regulatory agencies.

Appendix - Requested by Tulare County Environmental Health (UPA)

RMP Program 3 Prevention Program Component

(q)(1) External Events Analysis Information  Types of Events Considered
The PHA considered potential natural, and human caused external events that could result in an accidental release of ammonia. The human-caused external events considered were accidents resulting from either operator error, intentional harm / sabotage caused by a disgruntled employee or act

of terrorism. The natural external events considered were earthquake, flooding, high and low temperatures, and fire. A Sacramento County CUPA checklist was used for the analysis and can be found in the PHA documentation. 

(q)(2) External Events Analysis Information  Estimated Magnitude of Events Considered
For this evaluation, the extent and impact of external events (such as earthquakes, floods, wildfires, or other natural or man-made disasters). The "magnitude or scope" means the team must consider:
	How severe the event could be
	What area or systems could be affected 
	How likely the event is, if known or available

This ensures that your PHA considers credible external threats that could cause or contribute to an accidental release of a regulated substance. This evaluation was documented using the checklist methodology. 

The scope of evaluation included structural integrity, utility reliability, and potential for system overpressure, equipment damage, or access issues. If recommendations are generated, they are tracked separately through the facilitys action item system.

Tulare County Environmental Health (UPA) has not required a seismic assessment of the refrigeration system currently. The PSI contains the codes and standards in place at the time of installation and at the time of modifications to the system, if applicable.

(q)(3) External Events Analysis Information  Offsite Consequence Potential

Beyond the regulatory requirement to assess only those external events with the potential to cause offsite consequences, all identified external events were evaluated. Associated process controls and mitigation systems for each event are summarized in the PHA documentation.
(q)(4) External Events Analysis Information  Date of Most Recent Field Inspection

The date of the most recent field verification that equipment associated with the refrigeration system is installed and maintained as designed was during the annual / five-year mechanical integrity insp

ection. Since all annual mechanical integrity inspections are completed by an outside contractor, each year is considered to meet the five-year independent mechanical integrity inspection. 

It shall be noted that the facility must complete a safety evaluation by January 2026 of the entire system per ANSI/IIAR 9, Standard for Minimum System Safety Requirements for Existing Closed-Circuit Ammonia Refrigeration Systems. By completing this, it will meet this requirement.
